tldr: vLLM announced day-0 support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on Oct 15, covering image, document and video input through OpenAI-compatible serving. OrcaRouter comparisons against Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp followed on Oct 16, and NVIDIA added speech with Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe on Oct 28.
whats_new: AWS published a guide on Oct 29 for deploying Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B-parameter mixture-of-experts model, on Amazon EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS.
why_it_matters: Nemotron 3.5 now has a managed-Kubernetes deployment path on AWS alongside vLLM serving, so the decision shifts from whether you can host it to whether self-hosting beats a metered API.

status.detail: Servable on vLLM since launch day; speech added Oct 28 and an AWS EKS/HyperPod deployment guide followed Oct 29.

beats.headline: vLLM ships day-0 support for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
beats.summary: Multimodal serving (image, document, video) with OpenAI-compatible endpoints and multi-token prediction.

beats.headline: OrcaRouter pits it against Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp
beats.summary: Three write-ups in one day, centered on metered pricing versus downloadable weights.

beats.headline: Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2 add multilingual speech
beats.summary: NVIDIA's Hugging Face post presents a transcription model you can prompt and adapt, with the Granary v2 dataset.

beats.headline: AWS documents Nemotron deployment on EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS
beats.summary: AWS describes the 120B mixture-of-experts model's architecture and use cases, then walks through deploying it.

open_questions: Do independent benchmarks confirm the index-point gaps OrcaRouter reports against DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp?
Will other clouds or inference engines besides vLLM and AWS add Nemotron 3.5 Super VL?
Does Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe get vLLM or other OpenAI-compatible serving support?
take_for_builders: If you run multimodal document or video agents on AWS, compare the EKS/HyperPod path with your existing vLLM deployment on your own eval; for voice pipelines, test Transcribe on your own multilingual audio before swapping out your current ASR.
